newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts lose on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts lose on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mixed Thursday in a moderate session, with front months losing more ground amid forecasts for more mild weather next week, industry sources said.
February skidded 11.4 cents to close at $2.794 per million British thermal units. March settled 10.3 cents lower at $2.533. Other deferred months ended mixed.

"The bull market is over for now. Cash looks terrible because of (mild) weather. Watch out for falling prices," said one Houston-based trader, adding mild weather was likely to keep physical and paper prices on the defensive near term.

While Wednesday's AGA data showed an unexpectedly large 262 bcf weekly stock draw that roused the bulls, traders said the impact of the report was blunted by forecasts for mostly above-normal U.S. weather later this month and next.
Technical traders said the steady climb in open interest in the previous five-day selloff was a bearish indicator that fresh shorts have entered the market.

While some said the market was oversold and due for a short covering bounce after a 22 percent dive in six sessions, few expected an upside move to be sustained. They pegged key support in February at the December 31 low of $2.613. Psychological resistance was seen at $3.00, with better selling likely at $3.33, $3.64 and then $3.80-3.84.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were five to 10 cents lower Thursday in the $2.90-2.95 area. Midcon pipes lost about a nickel to $2.80-2.85. New York city gate gas slipped five cents or more to about the $3.30 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 2.9 cents to $2.254. NYMEX said an estimated 52,475 Hub contracts traded, down slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 54,185.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas expires next Monday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Wednesday.

On KCBT, February closed 14.5 cents lower at $2.60, while most deferreds finished down by 1.5 to 7.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.1 cents to 19.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 361 contracts traded, down sharply from Wednesday's total of 1,194.
